maria: quick Q — doing a canary rollout for redwood-canary. Need to grab p50/p95/p99 TTFT and tokens/sec for last 30m for a quick oncall check. Where should I look (dashboards / queries / traces)?

henry: short pointers:
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency-explorer?var-service=redwood-canary -> panels: "TTFT distribution" (histogram), "Tokens/sec by route" and "Request percentiles (p50/p95/p99)". Use last 30m.
- PromQL examples:
  p95 TTFT: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{service=\"redwood-canary\"}[5m])) by (le))`
  tokens/sec: `sum(rate(redwood_tokens_served_total{service=\"redwood-canary\"}[1m]))`
- Traces: Jaeger search filter service=redwood-canary, look for traces with tag `route` and `cache_miss=true`: https://jaeger.internal/redwood/search?service=redwood-canary&limit=20
- Logs: Kibana dashboard "tokenflow-logs" or `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=redwood-canary --since=30m`

sam: +1 on checking prefix cache hit rate: metric `prefix_cache_hit_ratio{service=\"redwood-canary\"}`. If tokens/sec is fine but TTFT spikes, likely cache miss path or small-batch fallback. Also check `model_variant_fallback_count` for routing fallbacks.

anita: if you want quick sample traces, use the Jaeger API: 
```
curl -s 'https://jaeger.internal/api/traces?service=redwood-canary&limit=25&lookback=30m' | jq .
```
then open the top trace in the UI and inspect spans: `kv-cache`, `serve-loop`, `kernel-exec`. Filter by span duration > 200ms to find slow spots.

opsbot: ALERT: canary-ttft-p95 breached (rule: canary-ttft-p95 > 1.8s) — fired at 1712345805.

maria: ugh ok. Can someone suggest a short checklist to triage before I abort the rollout? I want to rule out noisy warmup vs real regression.

henry: quick triage checklist:
1) Confirm tokens/sec steady: check tokens/sec panel / PromQL above.
2) Check prefix cache hit ratio and KV cache warmup (metric `kv_cache_warmth{service=\"redwood-canary\"}`).
3) Inspect 5 slow traces in Jaeger for common span (kernel/compilation vs network).
4) Look at per-route p95 — isolate if single route causing spike.
5) If p95 > 1.5s but tokens/sec low, try a warmup run: `wrk -t4 -c8 -d60s http://canary.internal/route/X` to prefill caches.
6) If widespread p99 regressions, fallback traffic to stable variant (use rollout console).
I can open a small PR to relax the canary alert to 1.8s for the next 30m while you triage.

anita: log grep that helped me earlier: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=redwood-canary -c runner --since=15m | grep -E \"TTFT|token_rate|cache_miss\"` — look for repeated compilation warnings.

maria: thanks — please open the PR to mute/adjust the alert, and ping me. I'll run the warmup and collect 5 traces and paste links here.

henry: on it. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-alerts/pull/402 — adjusts canary p95 -> 1.8s for 30m and adds note to oncall runbook. I'll also pin the Grafana panels to the canary channel.

maria: awesome, thx. ping me when warmup finished. :thumbsup:
